tools.name: gaia_status
tools.description: Editor status: frame counter, game update time, whether time is advancing, project, selection, undo depth.

tools.name: gaia_eval
tools.description: Evaluate F# in Gaia's live interactive session on the editor thread (Prime, Nu, Nu.Gaia and the project are opened). `world`, `SelectedScreen`, `SelectedGroup`, `SelectedEntity` are bound when mentioned. Each eval snapshots the world first, so gaia_undo reverts its world changes (not files or FSI definitions). Returns kind ok|compile_error|runtime_error, FSI output, and diagnostics with line/column. Keep snippets small; a non-terminating eval freezes the editor (then use gaia_ping to confirm and gaia_restart to recover). timeout_s (default 30) bounds the wait; a timed-out eval cannot be cancelled. If Gaia's exception dialog is open (status.pendingException), call gaia_resolve_exception first.

tools.name: gaia_ping
tools.description: Liveness check answered off the editor thread (works while it is blocked): last frame, ms since that frame, the op currently running and for how long, queue length, unresponsive flag.

tools.name: gaia_resolve_exception
tools.description: Resolve Gaia's 'Unhandled Exception!' dialog (shown in status.pendingException after a frame threw): hard_rewind undoes the last edit; ignore keeps the world as-is. Most tools refuse while it is open.

tools.name: gaia_restart
tools.description: Kill and relaunch the headless Gaia this server started (same project). Use only when gaia_ping shows the editor unresponsive, e.g. after a non-terminating eval. Unsaved world state, undo history and FSI definitions are lost; project files on disk are untouched.

tools.name: gaia_undo
tools.description: Undo the last editor operation (including the world effects of the last eval).

tools.name: gaia_redo
tools.description: Redo the last undone editor operation.

tools.name: gaia_advance
tools.description: Run game time for N editor frames, then halt again (snapshotted; undoable).

tools.name: gaia_hierarchy
tools.description: List screens, groups and entities (depth-first) with dispatcher type names.

tools.name: gaia_inspect
tools.description: List a simulant's properties with types and values. Path: '' = game, 'Screen', 'Screen/Group', 'Screen/Group/Entity[/Child]'.

tools.name: gaia_screenshot
tools.description: Render 2 frames and capture the editor window as PNG. view=game hides editor chrome (Gaia capture mode) and restores it afterwards.

tools.name: gaia_frames
tools.description: Advance game time and capture a frame every `every` frames, `count` times; returns one contact-sheet PNG (left-to-right, top-to-bottom). Use to see motion/animation. Undo restores the pre-advance world.

tools.name: gaia_reload_code
tools.description: Hot-reload the project's F# source files from disk into the live world (Gaia F9). Returns the build log.

tools.name: gaia_log
tools.description: Editor log text after a given log sequence number (see gaia_status.logSeq).

tools.name: gaia_symbol
tools.description: Resolve a name (e.g. 'World.createEntity', 'Entity.SetColor', 'MyGame.MyDispatcher') in the live F# session, with the session's opens: F# signature for each overload, XML doc summary, and declaration file:line (read the source there when docs are thin).

tools.name: gaia_checkpoint
tools.description: Save a named checkpoint of the whole world (kept outside the undo stack; at most 16), restore one (restore=true; the restore itself is undoable), or delete one (delete=true). Use before risky edits, and with gaia_diff to see exactly what an edit or a run of game time changed.

tools.name: gaia_diff
tools.description: Compare the current world with a checkpoint: simulants added and removed, and every changed property with its value before and after (symbolic text). `limit` caps the changed list (default 200).

tools.name: gaia_assert
tools.description: Check an F# bool expression over `world` once per frame for `frames` frames (game time advances when frames > 1; undoable). Stops at the first false or exception and reports that frame. `probe` is an optional F# expression of any type, printed at the end or at the failure (e.g. a position). Example: predicate `(Simulants.Gameplay / "Scene" / "Ball").GetPosition world |> fun p -> p.Y > -300.0f`.

tools.name: nu_docs
tools.description: Search Nu API XML documentation (member ids and summaries) by regex/keywords. Returns up to `limit` members.
